q1_public_access.question: Is every data point publicly accessible without auth?
q1_public_access.notes: GSA eLibrary is the official public database of all GSA Schedule contracts. Data is public domain per FAR 9.105-2(b)(1). Direct bulk export available with no authentication. Federal procurement transparency regulations mandate public disclosure.

q2_pii.question: Does it contain PII (personal email, phone, home address, SSN, financial account)?
q2_pii.notes: Zero PII violations. All data is company/business entity information. Email field contains only 'maspmo@gsa.gov' (GSA Mass Acquisition PMO administrative contact, not contractor personal emails). All addresses are commercial business locations, not residential. No phone numbers, financial accounts, or individual-level data present.

q3_robots_tos.question: Is any source's robots.txt or ToS violated by our harvest method?
q3_robots_tos.notes: Government public records. GSA eLibrary provides direct export functionality. No ToS restrictions on redistribution (government data in public domain). No robots.txt violations - data accessed via official UI export feature.

q4_copyright.question: Are we reproducing copyrighted content verbatim?
q4_copyright.notes: Factual government procurement data. U.S. government works not subject to copyright (17 USC § 105). No copyrightable narrative content.

q5_dual_use.question: Is any field dual-use or sensitive (security vulns, weapon specs, medical advice)?
q5_dual_use.notes: Business regulatory and contract information. No security-sensitive, dual-use, or controlled export fields. NAICS codes and Schedule categories are publicly disclosed industry classifications.

q6_putnam_test.question: Could a reasonable person whose data appears here object (Putnam test)?
q6_putnam_test.notes: GSA Schedule contract holders have no expectation of privacy. GSA publishes this data specifically for procurement transparency and to facilitate teaming arrangements. Contractors voluntarily entered into public contracts knowing this information would be disclosed. No reasonable objection possible.

q7_gdpr_ccpa.question: GDPR/CCPA clean? Any EU/CA persons → ensure no PII, ensure right-to-erasure pathway.
q7_gdpr_ccpa.notes: Business entities with U.S. federal contracts. Not personal data under GDPR/CCPA. U.S. government public records. No personal data requiring erasure rights.

details.harvest_report_notes: This is a representative sample of GSA Schedule contractors. Full dataset of ~30,000 contractors can be harvested with extended run time (~4 hours).

blocking_issues.rationale: Product spec promises '30,000+ active GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract holders' in one_liner and pricing_rationale. Current dataset contains only 5 unique records (0.017% coverage). This is a sample/placeholder dataset, not a production-ready product. Per DataStructured hard rules: 'Production code only. No mocks, no placeholders, no half-built features in shipped products.' A 5-row sample masquerading as a 30,000-row product violates this rule and constitutes false advertising to buyers.
blocking_issues.required_action: Complete full harvest of ~30,000 GSA Schedule contract holders before shipping. Data-engineer must run extended 4-hour harvest. Data-steward must clean/dedupe full dataset. Then return to compliance-officer for re-audit.

ethics_verdict_summary: All 7 compliance questions PASS. Dataset is ethically clean: zero PII violations, 100% public domain government data, no auth requirements, no ToS violations, no copyright issues, no dual-use concerns, passes Putnam test, GDPR/CCPA compliant. HOWEVER: Product is materially incomplete (5 rows vs. 30,000 promised) and cannot ship in current state. This is a sample dataset, not a production product. Hard rule violation: 'No placeholders in shipped products.' Verdict: NEEDS_FOUNDER_REVIEW for decision on whether to complete full harvest or adjust product positioning/pricing to match sample dataset scope.
recommended_next_steps: OPTION 1 (RECOMMENDED): Data-engineer runs full 4-hour harvest to collect all ~30,000 contractors → data-steward cleans/dedupes → compliance-officer re-audits → ship as planned at $79
OPTION 2 (PIVOT): Reposition product as 'GSA Schedule Contract Holders Sample Dataset (5 verified records)' → reprice to $5-10 → ship immediately as educational/proof-of-concept product
OPTION 3 (ABORT): Abandon product due to 4-hour harvest time not justifying $79 price point given existing enterprise competitors
notes: Dataset ethics: 100% clean. Dataset completeness: 0.017% of promised scope. This is not a compliance FAIL (no ethical violations), but a product readiness FAIL (materially incomplete). Founder decision required on path forward. If full harvest approved, ethics re-audit will be trivial (same source, same structure, same compliance profile). Current 5-row sample demonstrates harvesting methodology works and produces clean, compliant data.
